s: a gritty postwar bargain strip under the railway tracks near Ueno
w: A dense market street running under the JR tracks between Ueno and Okachimachi, born as a black-market strip in the postwar rubble and still trading on the same raw energy. Dried seafood and spices, cheap clothing, and street snacks -- yakitori, takoyaki, crepes -- fill stalls that get louder and busier as evening comes on.
_facts: Runs along the JR railway tracks between Ueno and Okachimachi stations
Name derives from a postwar black market ("ame-ya" candy shops / "ame" American goods) that grew up here
Mix of dried-seafood and spice wholesalers, discount clothing stalls and street-food vendors
Busiest in late afternoon and evening
